Data_Source: Dutch Head and Neck Oncology Cooperative Group
Main_Finding: T3/T4 and incomplete resection worsened recurrence; T/N stage, high grade, and PNI worsened distant metastasis and OS

Population: High-grade and/or locally advanced major salivary gland tumors
Comparison: Surgery alone vs surgery plus radiotherapy
Main_Finding: Adjuvant radiotherapy was associated with improved survival in high-risk groups

Population: Salivary gland tumors treated with adjuvant IMRT
Comparison: IMRT with or without concurrent chemotherapy
Main_Finding: Postoperative IMRT was well tolerated and associated with high local control
Limitations: Nonrandomized; chemotherapy comparison susceptible to selection bias

Population: Major salivary gland carcinoma after postoperative radiotherapy
Main_Finding: Locoregional control was reasonable; distant metastasis remained dominant in high-risk subsets

Population: Head and neck salivary gland cancer after postoperative radiotherapy
Main_Finding: Postoperative radiotherapy supported local disease control; no strong global evidence for added CCRT benefit

Population: Primary parotid carcinoma treated with surgery and postoperative radiotherapy
Main_Finding: Positive margins, high grade, and T3/T4 reinforced the postoperative radiotherapy indication

Population: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of major salivary glands
Main_Finding: Long-term outcomes were favorable after combined local therapy
